meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with Islamic Sharia as a primary source of legislation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended (including by Law No. 36 of 2015), and its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 1936 of 2004; UBO disclosure obligations imposed under Articles 5 bis and 5 ter of the Executive Regulations of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by the Ministry of Investment and International Cooperation Decree No. 566 of 2019, requiring submission of ultimate beneficial ownership data to the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each shareholder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin of the shareholder/manager

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Conduct / police clearance certificate for each authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or written consent of the corporate shareholder approving incorporation and naming of local agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notarizing authority of the parent company

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming identity and financial standing of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-maintaining bank in the jurisdiction of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD under AML Law No. 80/2002 requires identification and verification of all beneficial owners, enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs), both foreign and domestic, and screening against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, Egyptian terrorist entity lists, and Egyptian Central Bank counter-terrorism directives. OFAC SDN screening is also mandatory for transactions clearing through US payment rails (Stripe, Authorize.Net); a failure to screen or identify sanctioned UBOs is grounds for suspension of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Online Services Portal – www.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be filed in Arabic and may be accompanied by an approved Latin-script transliteration. Arabic names must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. Pure-Latin names are not accepted unless a certified Arabic transliteration is provided and the Arabic form is available at first registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written grievance with GAFI's Legal Affairs and Complaints Unit within 15 working days of notification, attaching the original name reservation receipt and a statement of reasons. If the grievance is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Court (Council of State) within 60 days of the final rejection. During the appeal process, a distinct alternative name may be reserved without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a complete substitute. Egypt requires an actual registered office with a physical address and a lease contract acknowledged before a notary. A serviced office with a dedicated reception, meeting room, and administrative presence is acceptable if the company's management lawfully operates therefrom; a pure mail-drop virtual address will be rejected by GAFI.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 10% to 15% annual probability of unannounced inspection in the first operating year for a low-risk standard LLC, increasing to substantially higher levels if UBO reporting inconsistencies or sanctions network traffic are detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Arts. 43-47 and Executive Regulations); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (one-stop shop provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Incorporation Department / Commercial Registry Window
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Sharika wa Al-Nizam Al-Asasi)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for an Egyptian LLC; the share capital is fixed by the founders in the Articles of Association and must be fully subscribed. Contributions are paid into the corporate bank account or valued in-kind in accordance with the Companies Law. No mandatory escrow account is required at incorporation, but evidence of the capital contribution may be required by GAFI or banks at account opening.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation and organization of the Company, as set out in the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, are ratified. RESOLVED, that the issued share capital stated in the Articles is deemed fully subscribed and the contribution procedures satisfy applicable Egyptian company law. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address filed with GAFI, Egypt, and the office appears in all official documents. RESOLVED, that [Manager Name] is appointed as Manager and registered representative of the Company with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and submit statutory filings, and [Officer Name] is appointed Secretary and Finance Officer. RESOLVED, that the incorporation application be submitted to the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and the Commercial Registry, and each filing be executed under these authorities. RESOLVED, that all filing documents are hereby approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Trade Name Reservation and Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Sharikati Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed trading name in Arabic and English against existing registered names, and confirm the principal activity (ISIC 3240 / printing of collectible trading cards) is classified as a permitted GAFI/IDA activity. Submit three alternative names and the company business-activity description. Pay the name-reservation fee online or at the GAFI service window.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of each founder
Proposed trade name in Arabic and English
Project synopsis describing collectible trading card production scope
GAFI name-reservation request form duly signed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity to an existing mark, the applicant may re-file immediately with alternative names. If GAFI determines the activity requires prior IDA clearance, the applicant shall obtain a preliminary industrial licensing opinion and resubmit the application within 15 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice - General Notary Public (Toshih) Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Arabic-language Memorandum and Articles of Association before the notary. The notary shall verify founder identity, legal capacity, share allocation, registered office particulars, and manager appointment. The executed instrument must be stamped and signed by notarial officers to establish the statutory formation date.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Name reservation certificate issued by GAFI
Copy of lease contract or ownership deed for the registered office
Original IDs/passports of all founders and appointed managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary will issue a correction note identifying any defect. The founders shall amend the Articles by separate deed and re-execute the notarization; no new name-reservation fee is charged if the legal name is unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Dossier to GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation dossier through the GAFI one-stop shop. GAFI will verify the notarized Articles, legalize the foundation documentation, and issue the provisional incorporation certificate and a reference number for commercial registration. This step combines the initial company registration, tax card registration, and municipal registration into the one-stop process where electable.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI name-reservation certificate
First board resolution appointing manager and secretary
Registered office lease contract and proof of address
Founder identification documents and bank statement if capital deposit is shown
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a queried application, the applicant must respond to GAFI comments within 30 days per the Investment Law. If GAFI requests documentary supplementation, the missing dossiers must be filed electronically; if substantive legal amendments are required, the Articles must be re-notarized and a revised application submitted without additional government incorporation fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Extract and Company Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office at GAFI / Egyptian Tax Authority Registration Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the commercial registry formality to receive the official commercial registry extract (al-qayd altijari), company identification number, and certified formation decision. Immediately after issuance present the extract to the Egyptian Tax Authority to obtain the tax card and corporate income tax/witholding tax registration for the LLC. The tax registration should identify VAT status based on the anticipated printing input/outputs and customs code for paper and foil.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Commercial registry application form
Notarized Articles and name certificate
Copy of manager identification and board resolution
Tax registration declaration form and lease evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry annotates the file with legal objections, the applicant may submit the notarial certificate and GAFI direction to correct the entry. If tax-card issuance is delayed, a provisional taxpayer number is provided pending correction of declared addresses or manager identifiers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Egyptian Gazette and Public Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya) / GAFI Secretariat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the commercial registry extract, publish a statutory notice of incorporation containing the company name, registration number, object, capital, registered office, and manager identity. Submit proof of publication to GAFI to complete the formal public-formation requirement under the Companies Law.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry extract
Incorporation certificate
Arabic-language notice text drafted under the Executive Regulations
GAFI publication form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gazette proof is delayed, the applicant may re-engage the gazette office and submit an expedited online publication request. Any factual error in the notice must be corrected by filing a corrected notice at the applicant's cost; no effect on company validity occurs where GAFI approval remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration with Social Insurance and Labor Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) / Ministry of Manpower Local Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer and obtain the social-insurance contribution number and manpower file number. Submit the founder/manager appointment documents, commercial registry extract, tax card, and the registered office address. The employer registration must be completed prior to hiring staff or within the statutory deadline from the commencement of business, whichever is earlier.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry extract and tax card
Articles of Association and board resolution for manager appointment
Manager passport or national ID
Official notarized employment contract forms for any initial employees
Registered office lease contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is processed late or fails due to administrative delay, the Company may contest the delay notice by submitting the GAFI commercial-registration date as the commencement date. Where the Social Insurance Office imposes surcharges, the Company may pay the assessed amounts under protest and appeal to the NOSI grievance committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Ministry of Trade and Industry — Industrial Licensing Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License for Printing and Graphic Reproduction Activity (including security holographic foil printing for collectible trading cards)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Initial EIA Screening required. A full EIA report will be requested if production involves solvent-based inks, varnishing, or volatile organic compound (VOC) usage above EEAA screening thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Ministerial Decree Law 48 of 1982 and Ministerial Decree 92 of 2013 benchmark limits: pH 6-9, BOD ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 80 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L and oil/grease ≤ 10 mg/L. VOC and gaseous emissions shall meet ambient and workplace exposure limits under Law 4 of 1994 and its implementing decrees. All printing inks, solvent residues, foil offcuts and chemical waste must be segregated and managed as hazardous or non-hazardous waste in accordance with the Egyptian Waste Management Law 202 of 2020.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The printing and foil-lamination facility must obtain a Civil Defense clearance certificate confirming fire-resistant construction, emergency egress, fire alarm/suppression systems, and safe storage of inks and solvents. A structural load inspection certificate is required from the local municipality for machine loads and occupancy. Occupational workplace clearance must be issued by the Ministry of Manpower after verification of ventilation, machine guarding, chemical safety data sheets, and personal protective equipment protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) within the Ministry of Finance; official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; integrated e-invoicing and e-receipts platform: https://einvoice.eta.gov.eg; corporate registration gateway: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – https://www.gafi.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A foreign parent incorporates the Egyptian LLC through GAFI's One-Stop Shop; the investment file receives a provisional tax file number simultaneously with commercial registration. Step 2: File the 'Tax Card' (Bayan) application with the competent ETA directorate using ETA Form 01/10, attaching notarized and Arabic-translated articles of association, GAFI investment certificate, commercial registration extract, board resolution/power of attorney, passport copies of shareholders/managers, proof of registered office (lease/utility), and the tax file opening declaration. Step 3: Open a corporate bank account with an Egyptian-licensed bank (or register a non-resident FX account for a foreign company without local establishment). Step 4: ETA reviews and issues the consolidated Tax Card containing a single TIN (unified for income tax, VAT, salary tax, and withholding tax). Step 5: If actual or expected annual taxable supplies reach EGP 500,000, complete VAT registration within 30 days of exceeding the threshold; non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Egypt (including via reverse charge) must register with the ETA's non-resident registration desk. Total statutory timeframe: approximately 30 working days from complete documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Egyptian LLC is a taxable legal person under Law 91/2005; no pass-through treatment); Territorial_Scope: Worldwide for Egyptian-resident LLCs (resident = incorporated in Egypt or central management/control in Egypt); Tax_Exempt_Zone: Not applicable to a standard non-free-zone LLC unless it obtains a specific free-zone/SEZ license from GAFI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a check-the-box or pass-through election for LLCs. Available statutory elections: (i) simplified SME regime under Law 91/2005 (turnover up to EGP 20 million: presumptive 0.4%–1.5% turnover tax) elected in the annual tax return; (ii) Article 53 deemed-profit election for non-resident contractors/consultants deriving service income from Egypt; (iii) tax-neutral restructuring election for qualifying mergers/demergers; (iv) free-zone/SCZone income-tax exemption only by express GAFI licence (not presumed). No hybrid mismatch election available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) governed by Law 67/2016, Executive Regulations (Decree 138/2017), and ETA circulars
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 (annual value of taxable supplies of goods and services; voluntary registration permitted at EGP 100,000)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory for all VAT registrants: B2B e-invoices must be transmitted in near-real-time to the ETA's clearance engine via REST APIs (integration profile) or the web portal for small taxpayers; ETA validates the invoice and returns a unique UUID and 2D QR code (digital stamp) that must be printed/transmitted on the document; no e-invoice QR means the deduction is disallowed. Since 2024, the e-receipt platform covers B2C transactions (payment-card and POS flows). Non-compliance penalties apply per invoice and per day of delay; taxpayers must use the ETA 'my invoices' worklist, update product codes (custom harmonized codes), and archive XML-based e-invoices for 5 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available for: (i) physical export of collectible trading cards and associated security holographic print products where the goods are actually shipped out of Egypt under a customs export declaration; and (ii) export of services (e.g., offshore printing/design royalties or overseas distribution rights) rendered to non-residents who are outside Egypt and not benefiting from the services inside Egypt. Qualifying conditions: seller must be a VAT-registered exporter; the contract/invoice must evidence export; goods must leave Egypt within the CBE allowed period; the export proceeds must be received in freely convertible foreign currency through Egyptian banks and repatriated within 180 days; services must be proven to be wholly performed or consumed outside Egypt. Taxable person must hold a valid export certificate and file VAT returns claiming zero rate; input VAT relating to export sales is credited/refundable with statutory priority.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Cargo Export Manifest) issued by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for airfreight exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate / FX Credit Advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in Egypt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA cross-matches e-invoices, customs export declarations (the ASYCUDA cargo system) and CBE bank FX records via the 'Tahweel' data exchange. If the 180-day repatriation date is missed, or the export declaration is missing/fraudulent, ETA will claw back the zero-rate benefit and issue an assessment equal to 14% VAT plus late-payment interest of 2% per month on the unpaid tax (minimum EGP 50/month), and a non-deduction penalty up to EGP 5 million under Law 67/2016 Art. 66; deliberate evasion can attract criminal fines of 1–3 times the tax amount and imprisonment (Art. 74 of Law 67/2016). Directors/founders are jointly and severally liable and the exporter's VAT refund file will be suspended.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the exclusive monetary and foreign-exchange regulator under Law No. 88 of 2003 (Banking and Monetary System Law), as amended by Law No. 18/2019, acting in coordination with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) for investment inflows and with the Ministry of Finance for external borrowing; CBE supervises licensed banks, interbank FX clearing, AML/CFT execution under Law No. 80 of 2002, and balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a soft managed-float foreign-exchange regime post 3 November 2016: the EGP/USD rate is formed in the CBE-supervised interbank market without administrative parity; current-account convertibility is broadly available for goods, services, dividends, interest, and royalties provided that the receiving or remitting bank validates the underlying commercial documents and records the correct balance-of-payments code. Capital-account transfers are permitted without CBE prior approval for foreign investors holding a GAFI investment certificate, but inward equity injection and outward repatriation are processed only after bank KYC, Commercial Registry (DERAT) verification, Tax Card and audited financial statement scrutiny; dividends are subject to the applicable dividend withholding tax under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and may be reduced by double taxation treaties where available. Residual profit-remittance hurdles are bank compliance artifacts: mismatched invoice descriptions, missing board dividend resolutions, unverified UBO passports, and inconsistent BoP code capture; each is mitigable through a standard remittance dossier comprising the GAFI certificate, audited distributable reserves, customs export declarations, and a consolidated banking confirmation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory repatriation timeline: 6 calendar months from the date of shipment (bill-of-lading date) for merchandise exports, maintained by the CBE in its consolidated forex instructions applicable to exporters; 100 percent of gross export proceeds must be credited to an EG_LLC account at a CBE-licensed bank in Egypt before the deadline, including proceeds generated through card-acquiring platforms that are cleared into Egyptian bank channels. Mandatory surrender ratio: zero percent — the CBE abolished forced conversion after the 2016 flotation, so funds may be retained in USD/EUR accounts, applied to import payments, or converted to EGP through the interbank market at the prevailing rate. Non-repatriation within the six-month window triggers bank-led penalty notifications, possible inclusion in the CBE defaulters list, restrictions on future export customs declarations, and tax-audit scrutiny of offshore receivables; relief is granted only with documented carrier or tracking evidence, SWIFT cover records, and a written explanation accepted by the account bank before customs enforcement blocks further shipments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Qatar National Bank Alahli (QNB Alahli) S.A.E.
Bank of Alexandria S.A.E. (Intesa Sanpaolo Group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for offshore digital e-money institutions (EMIs) operating as the primary Egyptian treasury rail; MEDIUM as a technical card-acquiring route for the stated Stripe/Authorize.Net rails when mounted on a licensed local PSP-aggregator architecture. Legal constraints: CBE e-money and payment service provider licensing under the amended Banking Law requires the payment issuer or acquiring entity operating in Egypt to be a CBE-licensed domestic corporate with registered capital and a physical presence; offshore EMIs holding UK/FCA or EU licenses are not recognised as eligible clearing partners for Egyptian export-proceeds repatriation and cannot open the required local account, hold foreign currency in-country, or issue EGP e-money. Therefore, EG_LLC should contract an Egyptian PSP (Paymob, Fawry, eFinance) or a card-network licensed local acquirer to settle Stripe/Authorize.Net transactions into the EG_LLC operational bank account; where cross-border retail volume is financially material, a foreign interposed sales entity becomes necessary to avoid violating the export-proceeds repatriation window, but the commodities sold and the end-use substance must correspond to the print-and-manufacture business scope.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch presence is effectively mandatory for initial corporate account opening in Egypt. All authorised signatories and each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) with a direct or indirect holding of 25 percent or more of EG_LLC must attend an in-person signature-verification and fraud-awareness interview at the chosen bank branch; biometric passport check, board resolution certification, and entity document originals (Commercial Registry extract, tax card, memorandum of association, GAFI card where applicable) are inspected against a CBE-mandated KYC checklist. Remote video or channel opening is available only to natural persons at fully licensed digital banks; no Egyptian Tier-1 bank permits a first-time LLC account without a local manager signature, unless the manager acts under notarised and apostilled powers of attorney executed in a foreign jurisdiction; in that case the UBO must still be present in the country or direct the interview through embassy-certified documentation that the compliance officer may reject at discretion. An accelerated opening path exists via selected banks' international desks with pre-checked group references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO-chain opacity: owner(s) resident abroad and the EG_LLC manager acting under a foreign power of attorney with no local executive director physical presence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified DERAT extract; updated GAFI registration; executed and apostilled board resolution; notarised powers of attorney; comprehensive UBO declaration with passport copies and proof of residence; source-of-wealth letter from each shareholder's home bank; audited good-standing certificates; corporate register excerpts from the shareholder jurisdiction translated by an Egyptian certified translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Stripe/Authorize.Net settlement splits: card-rail receivables arriving through offshore PSPs and mismatching the B2B trade invoices or lacking export-customs correlation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full merchant-service agreements; platform settlement reports with transaction-level reconciliation; commercial invoices cross-referenced to Stripe charge IDs; logistics and carrier waybills evidencing cross-border delivery; customs declaration C21 records; a documented treasury reconciliation policy committing all PSP net settlements to the repatriated export proceeds ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Security holography and cold-foil printing flagged as sensitive dual-use manufacturing or sanctions-screened supply equipment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: HS classification certificate (Chapter 49 printing and collectable card categories); product end-use attestation restricting sales to hobby-trading-card channels; GOEIC import/export confirmation where registrable; supplier declarations proving foil, ink, and hologram inputs are of non-sanctioned origin; internal compliance register covering all counterparties against UN/EU/US sanctions lists; transaction-level screening logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate advance payments or royalty/licensing income credited to a low-capital LLC before export deliveries occur.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed print-distribution and brand-licence agreements; purchase orders specifying advance clauses; remittance advices referencing contracts; forward-hedge confirmations; draft audited financial statements recording advances as liabilities; GAFI investment certificate where inbound remittances are booked as equity; cash-flow treasury policy distinctly separating customer advances from capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Seasonal cash-intensive local trading-card resale producing EGP cash deposits exceeding accounted retail revenue without an audit trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS and merchant-acquiring statements; shop-level retail invoices and VAT records; customs documentation for packaging inputs; a board-adopted cash-management policy capping EGP cash deposits at EGP 100,000 per day; external auditor signed confirmations; weekly reconciliation matrix aligned to Tax Authority filings and product-release events.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing sequence: (1) EG_LLC shareholder meeting adopts the capital increase; (2) the foreign shareholder transmits a SWIFT MT103 from its home bank to the EG_LLC account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank with the purpose code corresponding to Direct Investment in Egypt — Equity Capital (BPM6 A8) and a payment reference equal to the GAFI certificate and board resolution numbers; (3) the receiving bank conducts inflow verification — Commercial Registry extract, GAFI investment certificate, notarised memorandum, board resolution, UBO and sanctions screening — and credits the funds either to the capital contribution or deposit sub-account or to the operational USD account; (4) settlement completes through the CBE RTGS platform for the EGP leg or through a correspondent banking network (for example CIB or HSBC USD Nostro via J.P. Morgan or Citi) for the hard-currency leg; (5) after credit confirmation, the Commercial Registry and the Tax Authority are updated to certify the capital increase, and the bank files the BoP statement with the CBE. The remitter must never instruct the Egyptian bank to convert the equity proceeds to a fixed EGP rate; conversion, if requested, is executed at the interbank rate upon treasury desk instruction only, to avoid black-market records; all MT103 messages must use the exact legal name EG_LLC in field 59 to preserve the audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails ranked per value and counterparty: (a) SWIFT MT103/MT202 bank transfers for mid-value import payments — holographic films, cold-foil substrate, inks, varnish, packaging board, cutting dies, tools, and royalty or licence fees; these are cleared through the Egyptian bank's correspondent network (USD via CHIPS/Fedwire correspondents such as J.P. Morgan, HSBC or Citi; EUR via TARGET2 used by a European correspondent); (b) commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 with ISBP 745 practice for high-value equipment and large print-supplier contracts, opened by the Egyptian account bank and confirmed by an international bank; (c) standby letters of credit or bank guarantees where a foreign supplier demands performance assurance; (d) local EGP supplier settlements through the CBE RTGS same-day clearing rail. Every outbound disbursement requires the underlying pro-forma or commercial invoice, customer and supplier KYC certification, customs declaration where goods are physically imported, and a purpose code matching the CBE balance-of-payments matrix; the bank may request the final landed-cost audit file for a disbursement exceeding the transaction threshold, but no central-bank pre-approval is required for genuine documented trade settlements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP FX forward (synthetic forward executed at the interbank market rate with matured two-sided cashflows), available to EG_LLC on the strength of a genuine export or import contract, standard tenor up to 12 months, governed by a CBE-licensed bank master agreement and typically collateralised with a 10 to 20 percent margin or initial-deposit requirement.

USD/EGP FX swap (short-dated swap through simultaneous spot and forward legs) for treasury liquidity smoothing and pledge-free EGP working capital bridging; maturities normally capped at one month with rollover by bilateral bank approval.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing the EGP and settled in USD outside Egypt; permissible only through an offshore treasury or special-purpose vehicle because CBE-licensed banks are prohibited from booking NDFs domestically; used as an economic hedge of EGP-denominated receivables with the underlying exposure documented in the offshore treasury policy.

USD/EGP cross-currency swap (or EUR/EGP) aligned to long-term export financing or major equipment-purchase debt service; execution requires ISDA/CSA documentation and CBE aggregate-position reporting, with availability generally limited to first-tier corporate clients using the largest Egyptian banks.

Unilateral USD/EGP currency options (call or put, either vanilla or zero-premium formula) offered by international banks through the licensed treasury desk of a domestic bank as embedded in export-financing structures, not as standalone speculative products; premium paid in USD through a foreign custodian may require Egyptian BoP reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ETA Form No. 4) for the LLC, including final tax computation and payment of corporate income tax due
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four (4) months of the fiscal year-end; for a standard calendar-year LLC, file and pay by 30 April annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex-officio assessment plus additional penalty of up to 10% of the assessed tax; late or unpaid amounts accrue interest at 2% per month or fraction from the due date; enforcement includes bank attachment and tax criminal proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement and auditor's report) and annual company registry declaration filed with GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General assembly approval within three (3) months of fiscal year-end; GAFI filing within six (6) months of the fiscal year-end (calendar-year LLC: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning followed by fine of approximately EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 (~USD 100 to USD 1,050); persistent non-filing for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off proceedings and suspension of the commercial registry record

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the LLC's commercial registration record, confirming company particulars, managers, registered office and paid-up capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry, filed through the integrated GAFI/Commercial Registry electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the month of January (1 to 31 January) of each calendar year, renewing the record for the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs administrative fines of approximately EGP 100 to EGP 1,000 and blocks issuance of commercial certificates; continued non-renewal leads to removal from the Commercial Register and strike-off of the LLC

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Statement and confirmation of the Register of Members, including the log of share transfer deeds executed during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Beneficial Ownership Database, accessible to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, bundled with the audited financial statements filing within six (6) months of fiscal year-end; any share transfer or beneficial ownership change must be notified to GAFI within fifteen (15) days of execution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines imposed on the LLC and responsible managers for failure to maintain or update the UBO register, with penalties up to EGP 100,000 and imprisonment for willful false declarations under AML Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended; persistent breach supports administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for every Egyptian limited liability company without size exemption: the annual general assembly must appoint one or more independent certified public accountants registered under Law No. 40 of 1978 and accepted by the Egyptian Tax Authority; no minimum capital or turnover relief applies under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued under Ministerial Decree No. 110 of 2015, substantially converged with IFRS; statutory financial statements prepared in Egyptian pounds with narrative in Arabic; IFRS permitted for group reporting and regulated entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, and upon every share transfer, the LLC must update the Register of Members and the Beneficial Ownership Register and confirm the same to GAFI; share transfers require an authenticated transfer deed consistent with the LLC's articles, entry into the Members Register, and a GAFI/Commercial Registry update within 15 days; the annual confirmation is filed together with the audited financial statements package
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders ledger with transfer records)
Minute Book of General Assemblies and Management Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 800 per year (licensed compliance agent and registered-office package in Greater Cairo)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 - USD 3,000 per fiscal year for a small or medium manufacturing LLC, depending on inventory complexity, related-party volumes and export activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday. Eligible incentives under Investment Law No. 72/2017: 50% deduction of qualified investment costs for SMEs/new projects in designated governorates; SCZone licensed projects may enjoy negotiated incentives (up to 50% deduction of invested capital) during a specified exploitation period. Standard statutory allowances include depreciation per Schedule of Law No. 91 of 2005, interest deduction, and charitable donation deduction up to 5% of net profit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 45 – Corporate Income Tax Return for Juridical Persons; transmitted via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (tax.gov.eg) with paper copy held by registered accountant.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year LLC, no later than 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter ETA-issued tax card number and commercial registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian LLC's tax ID; foreign shareholders' IDs are not entered here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, registered address, main activity (ISIC 3240 / collectible trading card manufacture with security holographic cold-foil printing).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm Egyptian registered address for service; place of effective management must be documented as Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State fiscal period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adopt the Egyptian LLC's statutory books year; do not align automatically with foreign parent's year-end unless ETA approves.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all sales of trading cards, printing services and related publishing income; include export revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply worldwide income taxation at the LLC level; consolidate only subsidiary entities legally merged in Egypt, not foreign owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs: specialty paper, cinema-grade foil, holographic cold foil, inks, dies, labor and factory overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support by customs declarations and supplier invoices; transfer pricing adjustments from related-party purchases must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent, wages, utilities, insurance, freight, marketing and administrative expenses that are real, ledgered and incurred for the business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct foreign head-office general costs absent an Egyptian cost-sharing or recharging agreement with economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back statutory non-deductibles: personal withdrawals, fines, bribe payments, unverified telecommunication/entertainment categories, and contested tax penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to non-resident related parties are allowable only to the extent arm's-length and documented under Articles 30-34 of Law No. 91 of 2005.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result after reconciliations; if loss, record the amount for five-year carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A controlled foreign corporation (CFC) reallocation is not applied to the Egyptian LLC itself; the LLC must still substantiate its local substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply 22.5% statutory CIT rate to taxable income; include surcharge taxes if any special industrial/commercial levy applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax entirely at LLC level; non-resident shareholders have no direct Egyptian filing obligation for distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct quarterly provisional installments, WHT credits, and any foreign tax credit in accordance with Article 38 of Law No. 91 of 2005.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach DTA-based foreign tax credit calculations and TRC if claiming treaty relief on dividends, interest or royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter final tax due/refund; declaration signed by director and licensed tax accountant (Tax Identification Number).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident-owned LLC must simultaneously report cross-border related-party transactions and confirm transfer pricing documentation is in place.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge on the tax due (statutory monthly range of 2%–5%, capped at 30%), an administrative fine up to EGP 10,000 for juridical persons, and automatic best-judgment assessment by the ETA. False declarations trigger evasion penalties in addition to the surcharge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate on dividends, interest or royalties, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Egyptian withholding agent: (1) valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state and notarized/apostilled in accordance with the DTA; (2) certified certificate of residence for the relevant year; (3) beneficial ownership declaration and shareholding structure forms; and (4) request for reduced WHT filed via the ETA's treaty relief procedure before payment. The Egyptian LLC is required to retain the original/electronic proof and apply the domestic 10% dividend WHT if treaty relief is not timely recognized.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT: 20% on interest and 20% on royalties paid to non-residents (reduced under applicable DTA; treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and 0% to 20% for royalties). Payments routed through a conduit without beneficial ownership will not receive treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 5,000,000 for controlled related-party transactions triggering a Local File; Master File and CbCR reporting are obligatory when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds EGP 15,000,000,000, as set by the Egyptian TP Decree (Ministerial Decree No. 577 of 2020).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply a GCC-style 'Economic Substance Regulation'; however, the Egyptian tax authority applies the abuse-of-law doctrine, sham transaction doctrine, and the beneficial ownership requirement embedded in Law No. 91 of 2005 and anti-avoidance case law. A licensed printing/manufacturing LLC must maintain actual premises, staff, equipment, bank account, stock and management decision-making in Egypt to be recognized as a taxable resident company and to obtain treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting holographic card sales revenue, overstating cost of goods sold, preparing two sets of accounting books, or submitting forged invoices/export records to ETA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of not less than 100% of the evaded tax and legal imprisonment; in aggravated cases, the fine reaches double the tax evaded; interest and late payment surcharges run to 30%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/signatories who participate or conspire in filing false returns are personally subject to criminal conviction, joint and several civil liability for restitution of the evaded tax, and travel bans under criminal/administrative enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling trading cards to a non-resident related distributor without arm's-length pricing, not preparing Local File when controlled transactions exceed EGP 5,000,000, or engaging in a structured arrangement with no real Egyptian production staff or premises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may re-determine the profit by arm's-length adjustment, disallow expense deductions, impose the 22.5% CIT on the adjusted profit, plus late payment surcharge and a penalty of up to 10% of the incorrectly priced transactions under TP enforcement practice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute export/import pricing at artificial margins can be assessed as tax representatives personally, with veil-piercing where the LLC is found to be a façade; director travel bans are available in tax debt recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing and concealing an LLC with no real office, no Egyptian bank operations, no employees, or a nominal capital used solely to shift profits out of Egypt or to treat personal costs as corporate expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may disregard the entity for income tax purposes, attribute its income to the Egyptian permanent establishment or beneficial owner, refuse VAT input credits, and impose evasion penalties plus court-ordered annulment in appropriate cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Court-piercing of the corporate veil substitutes personal property liability of directors/shareholders for corporate tax debts, exposes them to denunciation of fake inventories, and may include imprisonment for fraud if third-party creditors were misled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving proceeds through anonymous wallets or opaque payment rails, failing to maintain KYC/CDD files for large card distributors, using shell intermediaries outside Egypt, or omitting the beneficial owner from ETA and AML authority declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian AML Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended): financial penalties up to EGP 1,000,000 and imprisonment for 6 months to 7 years for CDD breaches; for proven money-laundering of proceeds, imprisonment not less than 3 years and a fine of EGP 100,000–1,000,000, plus confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and accountants are personally liable for failure to file suspicious transaction reports; travel bans, asset freezing orders and criminal imprisonment apply to those who knowingly facilitate or conceal offshore beneficial ownership.
